name: Embalming
overview: Scripture reveals that embalming was a practice learned by the Jews during their time in Egypt, as seen in Joseph commanding the physicians to embalm his father Israel and himself (Genesis 50:2, 26). This process involved a set period of forty days for embalming, after which mourning followed, reflecting Egyptian customs (Genesis 50:3). While embalming was customary in some cases, it was not universally practiced, as demonstrated by the burial of Jesus, who was wrapped in linen and anointed with spices rather than embalmed (Mark 15:46; 16:1). These passages highlight both the cultural influences on Jewish burial practices and the unique manner in which Christ's body was prepared, underscoring God's sovereign purpose in His death and resurrection.
